title: How to create a new project in Xcode on Mac: simple steps for Xcode 27
metaTitle: How to create a new project in Xcode on Mac
description: Learn how to create a new project in Xcode on Mac with this step-by-step guide. Master the Xcode 27 interface and start your app development journey today.
targetKeyword: how to create a new project in xcode on mac
intro: To create a new project in Xcode on Mac, launch the application and click Create a new Xcode project in the welcome window. You can also press Command + Shift + N or navigate to File > New > Project in the menu bar.
tldr: Open Xcode and select Create a new Xcode project.
Choose your target platform and template.
Configure project settings like product name and organization identifier.
Select your save location and enable Git repository.
Click Create to start your new development environment.

blocks.text: Xcode 27 is the current standard for Apple platform development. It requires macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later to run effectively. When you first open the app, you see a welcome screen. This screen offers a quick entry point to your work. Click the button labeled Create a new Xcode project to begin the setup process. If you have a project already open, use the menu bar instead. Go to File > New > Project to trigger the same assistant.

Once you initiate the project creation, a new sheet appears. This sheet displays various platforms including iOS, macOS, and visionOS. Choose the platform that matches your goal. Under each platform, you will see templates categorized by type. The Application category is the most common choice for new developers. Select the App template to build a standard application. Click Next to proceed to the configuration phase. Remember that developing for visionOS requires a Mac with Apple silicon.

The next screen requires specific details about your app. Enter a Product Name that identifies your work. The Organization Identifier follows a reverse domain style, such as com.yourname. Choose your interface, such as SwiftUI, and your language, usually Swift. These settings define how your code is structured. Always double check these fields before clicking Next. Incorrect naming here can make future refactoring more difficult.

The final step is choosing where to store your project. Select a folder on your Mac that is easy to find. Make sure the option to Create Git repository on my Mac is checked. This enables version control immediately. Version control is essential for managing changes as you code. Once you click Create, Xcode builds the directory structure and opens your new workspace.

Xcode can sometimes act strangely after creating a new project. You might encounter indexing errors or broken code completion. These are often due to corrupted cache files. A common fix is to perform a clean build. Go to Product > Clean Build Folder or use the shortcut Command + Shift + K. If that does not work, you can manually remove the Derived Data folder. Use the command rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData in your Terminal to clear it out.

It is common to confuse Xcode with Xcode Cloud. Xcode is the desktop application you use to write your code. Xcode Cloud is Apple's CI/CD service for automated testing and building. You do not create projects in a web browser. You configure Xcode Cloud inside your local Xcode project settings. Apple provides 25 compute hours per month for free for members of the Apple Developer Program.

faq.question: Do I need an Apple Developer account to create a project?
faq.answer: You do not need an account to create and run projects locally on your Mac. You only need one if you intend to distribute your app on the App Store.

faq.question: Why is my Xcode project showing random errors?
faq.answer: Random errors are often caused by corrupted build data. Try cleaning your build folder with Command + Shift + K or deleting the Derived Data folder in your library.

faq.question: Can I use Xcode on a Windows computer?
faq.answer: No, Xcode is exclusive to macOS. You must use a Mac to run Xcode and build apps for Apple platforms.

steps.name: Launch Xcode
steps.text: Open Xcode from your Applications folder or use Spotlight search by pressing Command + Space and typing Xcode.

steps.name: Start new project
steps.text: In the welcome window, click the button that says Create a new Xcode project.

steps.name: Choose template
steps.text: Select your platform such as iOS or macOS, then choose the App template under the Application category.

steps.name: Enter details
steps.text: Fill in your product name, organization identifier, and select your interface and language preferences.

steps.name: Save project
steps.text: Choose a folder to save your project and ensure the Git repository box is checked, then click Create.

troubleshooting.problem: Xcode is showing random build errors
troubleshooting.fix: Perform a clean build using Command + Shift + K or delete the Derived Data folder.
Close Xcode, delete the Derived Data folder in your Library, and restart the application.
